transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-11 15:00 UTC | Duration: 49m
Attendees: Maya Lin (Redwood AE), Jared Coleman (Redwood SE), Anita Reddy (Redwood CSM); Priya Desai (CTO, Vestra), Ethan Morales (Lead Engineer), Sara Kim (PM), Luis Ortega (DevOps)
---
[00:00] Maya: hi everyone, thanks for hopping on. quick round-robin, we updated the board — hope the time still works.
[00:12] Priya: yep good, thanks. we tried the latest SDK yesterday and hit a couple of weird binding issues, so mostly here to sync on that and the structured output errors.
[00:22] Jared: yeah i saw the logs, thanks for sending, ethan — um there are two things, one is a namespacing edge where the client instantiates a global helper instead of per-request, and two the function calling hook isn't consistently returning the tool metadata, so the validation in your app fails.
[00:35] Ethan: mhm, exactly. on our side it's intermittent — maybe 1 out of 7 calls. not consistent, but enough to break the pipeline.
[00:45] Maya: ok, can you show the snippet you used? i pulled the gist you linked but the import path looks like an older pattern.
[00:50] Sara: yeah, we wired it via the app platform shim, something like require('@redwood/sdk') then we wrap it in a singleton. i think that's the problem, but wanted confirmation.
[01:05] Jared: right, the recommended pattern is per-invocation client scope when you rely on tool/function metadata being attached to the response — singletons keep stale transient state, especially around KV cache and the tool registry.
[01:20] Luis: when you say KV cache, do you mean the model key-value cache, or some sdk-level cache? i'm seeing both in the logs.
[01:28] Jared: the model KV cache — the LLM runtime keeps per-session KV for faster auto-regeneration, but the SDK also has a small in-memory request cache. singletons can cause the two to misalign, which shows up as missing tool attributes.
[01:40] Priya: ah okay that could explain it. on the structured output side, our schema validator throws when the tool call is missing the 'tool_id' field. sometimes the response is fine but often it's nested under an unexpected key.
[01:55] Maya: that's probably because the function-calling response shape changed slightly with a retry — the runtime will emit a fallback path if the primary kernel fails. we should make sure the SDK normalizes that shape.
[02:08] Ethan: is that a runtime thing or SDK? because in our staging the runtime is the hosted test instance you gave us.
[02:16] Jared: it's a combination. runtime might emit variant shapes under error conditions; SDK should flatten them into the stable contract. we're going to push a tiny patch that adds normalization and a namespaced client constructor.
[02:30] Sara: can we see that patch before you publish? we'd like to test locally.
[02:34] Maya: yes — we'll share a snippet today.
[02:38] Priya: great. also, on retries: our logic currently retries on 5xx, but we've seen partial success where content is generated but tool metadata missing; a retry just duplicates the output and compounds the problem.
[02:54] Jared: good point — for function/tool calls we recommend idempotency keys and a smarter retry that checks for presence of tool metadata; if metadata absent treat as a transient kernel glitch and retry once with a fresh KV warmup.
[03:08] Ethan: what does 'KV warmup' mean practically? we don't want large memory spikes in production.
[03:16] Jared: it's a lightweight prefix run — send a short warmup prompt that primes the KV for the sequence length you expect. doesn't need to be heavy; just a couple tokens. we can also use the SDK helper to do that automatically when you detect a cold client.
[03:30] Luis: hmm can we schedule that in a background worker? don't want extra latency on the request path.
[03:36] Jared: yes background warmup is the usual pattern — we can provide a small runnable example.
[03:40] [03:42] (crosstalk) Priya: also want to confirm SSO and SOC2 docs — we need them for procurement kickoff.
[03:48] Anita: i've uploaded the SOC2 artifact to the shared folder; i'll ping the legal contact as well.
[03:54] Maya: thanks anita. we'll also list the roles required for audit and give a short mapping sheet.
[04:02] Ethan: back to structured output — we saw one case where the SDK serialized the function result as a string with escaped quotes, so our JSON schema fails on parsing. could be double-encoding?
[04:18] Jared: that likely comes from our safe-serialize fallback path — when the runtime flags an uncertain parse, SDK returns a string to avoid a hard failure. we can add a flag to force strict parse and fail early if you prefer.
[04:32] Sara: would rather fail early in staging so we catch it. in prod we can flip to soft fallback for resilience.
[04:40] Maya: that aligns with our recommendations. we'll send an SDK snippet that exposes parseMode: strict|safe and a namespaced client constructor.
[04:50] Priya: perfect. next, telemetry — we need clearer error tags so our on-call can triage quickly. the current logs show generic 'tool_error' without context.
[05:02] Jared: yes we can instrument more context: include request-id, sdk-client-instance-id, runtime-kernel-id, and a short shape-diff hash so you can group similar failures. we'll also add a sample Kibana/ELK query.
[05:18] Ethan: that would help a lot. can you also surface token-level cost per request? our product team wants to see unit economics for different batch sizes.
[05:27] Maya: we can add per-request token breakdown in the SDK telemetry payload. note that hosted returns usage in the response header, but SDK can correlate to your request.
[05:35] Sara: on the subject of batching — we're experimenting with a 16 request micro-batch vs single-call. latency's better single-call for small requests, but cost was lower with batch. any guidance?
[05:48] Jared: tradeoff — batching reduces per-token overhead but increases tail latency. for interactive workflows we usually keep batch size small (2-4) and rely on prefix caching and KV warmups. for high-throughput async pipelines, larger batches are better.
[06:03] Priya: ok let's capture that as guidance in the integration guide.
[06:08] Luis: i want to surface a separate DevOps item — VPC peering to your private connector failed during our initial test, network team saw TLS handshake timeouts.
[06:18] Maya: thanks — is that in the network logs you shared?
[06:21] Luis: yes i posted trace to the shared drive. looks like MTU mismatch on the route from our transit gateway.
[06:28] Anita: we'll loop in infra support, we had a similar issue with another customer and it was an MTU route. i'll create a ticket with networking team and copy you.
[06:37] [06:39] (brief silence as folks check links)
[06:45] Sara: one more thing — can Redwood confirm data retention for request logs in the pilot? we need to make sure no PII is stored.
[06:53] Maya: default is 30 days for pilot logs, with PII redaction options. we can enable shorter retention and ensure redaction filters are active for your workspace.
[07:03] Priya: please do that. procurement wants proof.
[07:07] Maya: we'll send a config snippet and confirm once applied.
[07:10] Jared: quick note on the latency benchmark — for the staging run we'll syntheticize requests that follow your real payload distribution; we'll run with and without KV warmup and compare p50/p95/p99.
[07:23] Ethan: sounds good. what's the expected throughput we should provision?
[07:26] Jared: for the initial run 1k concurrent requests over 5 minutes should expose tail behavior. we'll also provide guidance on Dedicated vs Hosted cost at the end.
[07:35] Priya: ok good. timeline?
[07:37] Maya: patch and SDK snippet today, KV warmup experiment numbers by Jared next Tues (2026-11-17), latency benchmark week of 11/16, results sync the following Thursday.
[07:51] Sara: we will run the structured-output parser tests and post failing cases in the shared doc by 11/18.
[07:58] Luis: i'll follow up on the VPC ticket and attach the network traces.
[08:03] Anita: i'll push SOC2 proof and SSO contact today.
[08:07] Priya: anything else?
[08:09] Maya: quick recap — action items and owners (we'll paste into CRM). anything to add?
[08:15] Ethan: just one nit — on the SDK namespacing, will that change our imports significantly? we prefer minimal churn.
[08:22] Jared: minimal, it's mostly a constructor change. we will provide a migration patch and tests.
[08:28] Priya: thanks team, appreciate the quick turn.
[08:31] Maya: thanks everyone. we'll share the snippet and the SOC2 link; catch up after the benchmark.
[08:36] (meeting ends)
